title: A paper says image-editing agents fail when they keep retrying the same tool
friendlyTitle: A paper says image-editing agents fail when they keep retrying the same tool
summary: In a paper submitted on 29 October, Haiyang Xu and co-authors argue that image-editing agents are limited by the tools they can call and by what the judge can see. On their expert-annotated benchmark, a general-purpose editor produced no usable result in more than 40% of cases. Their system, EditAgent, sends each step to a general editor and to specialized methods, and attaches a verification record to each candidate. With those records, ordinary vision-language judges beat reward models trained for the job. Experts preferred the parallel candidates to step-by-step refinement in 78.5% of the comparisons they decided, at no more than half the judge calls. The paper says EditAgent improved two open-weight editors on three benchmarks.
friendlySummary: In a paper submitted on 29 October, Haiyang Xu and co-authors argue that image-editing agents are limited by the tools they can use and by what the judge can see. On a test marked by experts, a general editor produced no usable result in more than 40% of cases. Their system, EditAgent, tries a general editor and specialized tools on each step, and attaches a check record to each result. With those records, ordinary vision models beat judge models trained for the job. Experts preferred the side-by-side results to step-by-step fixes in 78.5% of the comparisons they decided, with no more than half the judge calls. The paper says EditAgent improved two open editors on three tests.
whyItMatters: This is not a switch in a photo app. If an agent is editing images for you, a second pass with the same tool is a weak repair. The practical claim is to make a few variants from the original, and to judge them with a close crop and a measurement, not by glancing at the full frame. The paper is the claim. It is not a product you can install from the abstract.
